correctness.rationale: Removing a scalar diagonal from each matrix leaves three independent coordinates; the target trace-zero coordinates are the three signed wedge minors. There is no division by two, and the scalar lifts contribute q^(2m). In dimension three the exterior-square action of SL_3 on the dual of R^3 is the inverse-transpose action using the volume form. A primitive vector completes to a basis, whose determinant can be corrected by scaling a different column, so each target valuation has one orbit, even for targets π^s times a primitive lift. Use h=π^s e1∧e2. For first factor u of valuation a<=s divide by π^a in R/(π^(m-a)); primitives in the quotient extend to a basis, so the wedge image is exactly the two-forms which wedge to zero with the divided primitive u. This condition is π^(s-a) times its third coordinate equal to zero, giving q^(s-a) choices there, all nonunits, and q^(2(m-a))-q^(2(m-a-1)) choices for the first two coordinates. The image has q^(2(m-a)) elements and each fiber q^(m+2a). Summing gives the stated nonzero count; for h=0 all vectors are eligible, with the zero first vector giving q^(3m) choices. The formulas are positive for every trace-zero target and all other targets are excluded by the trace identity over a commutative ring. The frozen checker is a bounded cross-product test, not an independent matrix multiplication or a proof at general q,m. The independent check python3 -B /workspace/reproduce_finite.py 2 exhausts 65,536 literal ordered matrix pairs in each of Z/4, F2[epsilon]/epsilon^2 and F4, including non-trace-zero targets and nonprime residue size. All counts agree; zero fibers are 6400, 6400, and 5056. The frozen checker was not run.

Substitution gives (q+1)(q^(3m+s-1)-q^(3m-2)); multiplying by q^(2m) is exactly the matrix law. There is no extra counting conjecture or ring restriction. The companion Fourier-support theorem itself is about a different transform; the implication uses its exact zero counts and elementary lifts and orbits, not a confusion of transforms.

value.rationale: A mixed-characteristic distribution for additive matrix commutators is a natural invariant, and its profile could be useful in place of mere surjectivity. Here the exact profile is a mechanical re-expression of verified all-quotient determinantal counts via uniform lifts and valuation orbits. No mathematically distinct exact invariant remains in this narrow claim; the alternate direct wedge count is not a substantive surviving result on its own.
